\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{عمر} (umr)}{عمر (umr)}]{\ur{عمر} (umr) — age}

\label{lesson:UR-C486-umr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to be brought up, then the Urdu for to dress (someone).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{عمر}}
\textbf{\ur{عمر}} — \emph{umr} — \textquotedblleft{}age\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میری} \ur{بہن} \ur{کی} \ur{عمر} \ur{دس} \ur{سال} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{merī bahan kī umr das sāl hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister is ten years old.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{عمر}} (\emph{umr}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ʿumr}, \textquotedblleft{}life, a lifetime\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{umr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{umr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{merī bahan kī umr das sāl hai.} — My sister is ten years old.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to be brought up, then the Urdu for to dress (someone), then say \emph{umr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{عمر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Age\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اکلوتا} (iklautā)}{اکلوتا (iklautā)}]{\ur{اکلوتا} (iklautā) — only (of a child)}

\label{lesson:UR-C486-iklauta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for age, then the Urdu for of age.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اکلوتا}}
\textbf{\ur{اکلوتا}} — \emph{iklautā} — \textquotedblleft{}only (of a child)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{اپنے} \ur{ماں} \ur{باپ} \ur{کا} \ur{اکلوتا} \ur{بیٹا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh apne māṅ bāp kā iklautā beṭā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He is his parents' only son.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اکلوتا}} (\emph{iklautā}) is inherited from \emph{ēkkalaputra}, \textquotedblleft{}an only son\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from the words for \textquotedblleft{}alone\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}son\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2507).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گزرنا} (guzarnā)}{گزرنا (guzarnā)}]{\ur{گزرنا} (guzarnā) — to pass (of time); to go by}

\label{lesson:UR-C486-guzarna-pass}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for of age, then the Urdu for only (of a child).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گزرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{گزرنا}} — \emph{guzarnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to pass (of time); to go by\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بچپن} \ur{کے} \ur{دن} \ur{جلدی} \ur{گزر} \ur{گئے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachpan ke din jaldī guzar gae.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The days of childhood went by quickly.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{سال} \ur{جلدی} \ur{گزرا}, \emph{voh sāl jaldī guzrā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{گزرنا}} (\emph{guzarnā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{guzar}, \textquotedblleft{}a passing\textquotedblright{}, made into an Urdu verb; \textbf{\ur{گزشتہ}}, \textquotedblleft{}last, previous\textquotedblright{}, is the time that has gone by.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{guzarnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{guzarnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bachpan ke din jaldī guzar gae.} — The days of childhood went by quickly.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for of age, then the Urdu for only (of a child), then say \emph{guzarnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{گزرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To pass (of time); to go by\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Looking After Someone to Growing Up}

\label{lesson:UR-R486-review-480-486}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for to visit the sick and nursing the sick.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to visit the sick, nursing the sick, looking after, to lay (someone) down, to cover someone up
  \item an easing, restored, to massage, to press gently, to warm a sore place
  \item to bathe (someone), to shave the head, a shave, to have (something) cut, to trim
  \item pregnant, to give birth to, to be born, birth, a newborn
  \item to raise a child, a lullaby, to rock, to feed, to give (someone) a drink
  \item childhood, mischief, lisping, to be brought up, to dress (someone)
  \item age, of age, only (of a child), to pass (of time), the prime of life
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To visit the sick? (\textbf{\ur{عیادت} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{iyādat karnā}.) Nursing the sick? (\textbf{\ur{تیمارداری}}, \emph{tīmārdārī}.) Looking after? (\textbf{\ur{نگہداشت}}, \emph{nigahdāsht}.) To lay (someone) down? (\textbf{\ur{لٹانا}}, \emph{liṭānā}.) To cover someone up? (\textbf{\ur{اوڑھانا}}, \emph{oṛhānā}.) An easing? (\textbf{\ur{افاقہ}}, \emph{ifāqā}.) Restored? (\textbf{\ur{بحال}}, \emph{bahāl}.) To massage? (\textbf{\ur{مالش} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{mālish karnā}.) To press gently? (\textbf{\ur{دبانا}}, \emph{dabānā}.) To warm a sore place? (\textbf{\ur{سینکنا}}, \emph{seṅknā}.) To bathe (someone)? (\textbf{\ur{نہلانا}}, \emph{nahlānā}.) To shave the head? (\textbf{\ur{مونڈنا}}, \emph{mūṅḍnā}.) A shave? (\textbf{\ur{شیو}}, \emph{shev}.) To have (something) cut? (\textbf{\ur{کٹوانا}}, \emph{kaṭvānā}.) To trim? (\textbf{\ur{تراشنا}}, \emph{tarāshnā}.) Pregnant? (\textbf{\ur{حاملہ}}, \emph{hāmilā}.) To give birth to? (\textbf{\ur{جننا}}, \emph{jannā}.) To be born? (\textbf{\ur{پیدا} \ur{ہونا}}, \emph{paidā honā}.) Birth? (\textbf{\ur{پیدائش}}, \emph{paidāish}.) A newborn? (\textbf{\ur{نومولود}}, \emph{naumaulūd}.) To raise a child? (\textbf{\ur{پرورش} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{parvarish karnā}.) A lullaby? (\textbf{\ur{لوری}}, \emph{lorī}.) To rock? (\textbf{\ur{جھلانا}}, \emph{jhulānā}.) To feed? (\textbf{\ur{کھلانا}}, \emph{khilānā}.) To give (someone) a drink? (\textbf{\ur{پلانا}}, \emph{pilānā}.) Childhood? (\textbf{\ur{بچپن}}, \emph{bachpan}.) Mischief? (\textbf{\ur{شرارت}}, \emph{sharārat}.) Lisping? (\textbf{\ur{توتلا}}, \emph{totlā}.) To be brought up? (\textbf{\ur{پلنا}}, \emph{palnā}.) To dress (someone)? (\textbf{\ur{پہنانا}}, \emph{pahnānā}.) Age? (\textbf{\ur{عمر}}, \emph{umr}.) Of age? (\textbf{\ur{بالغ}}, \emph{bāligh}.) Only (of a child)? (\textbf{\ur{اکلوتا}}, \emph{iklautā}.) To pass (of time)? (\textbf{\ur{گزرنا}}, \emph{guzarnā}.) The prime of life? (\textbf{\ur{شباب}}, \emph{shabāb}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
